answer: A claim of uniqueness must be accompanied by a proof that no other identity holds the same underlying resource, and the proof enumerates the possibility space rather than asserting absence, so a cloned identity cannot assert uniqueness without exposing the clone. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. Each identity claims an echo, publishes a hollow that no other holder can publish, and is checked against the falcon: a fleet sharing one echo cannot produce two valid hollow proofs, and the falcon records the collision.
